marketRegime: Choppy, mean-reverting 5-minute crypto regime with frequent small reversals (observed moves clustering in the 6-18bps range before reverting) — not a strong trending regime. This explains why moderate momentum signals (move10-20bps) fail at ~35% win rate: the move is often noise/mean-reversion fodder rather than true momentum continuation. Only larger moves (20+bps, which IS profitable at +$10.14/43 trades, 55.8% win) represent real directional signal. Peer agreement (all coins moving together) is actually a contrarian/negative indicator here, likely reflecting broad-market noise/pump-and-dump wicks rather than idiosyncratic alpha.

applied.reason: move20+ bucket is the only strongly profitable move-size band (+$10.14, 55.8% win over 43 trades) while move10-20 is a certified loser (-$33.47, 34.6% win). Raising the effective floor toward the 20bps threshold (bounded max 30) aligns entries with the proven-profitable band and reduces reliance on the veto system to clean up after the fact. Keeping it near current 22 with slight tightening to 20 is conservative but should be pushed higher if sample size permits in future cycles.

all-agree peer bucket (full consensus) is paradoxically a loser (-$18.99, 44.6% win over 112 trades) and is already flagged reduce_confidence by the lesson system. Raising the confidence floor slightly forces the model to require more than just peer-agreement to clear the bar, discouraging entries that score high purely on consensus-driven (but historically unprofitable) signals.

Observed stop-losses are firing around 0.19-0.25 bid, implying losses of roughly 55-75% of entry value per stopped trade (worst trade -$15.93). Tightening the stop_loss_bid threshold modestly to 0.30 would cut losing trades earlier, reducing average loss size given the setup's near-coinflip win rate (49%) in MOMENTUM.

Current min_edge of 0.06 still allows entries in the loss-making move10-20 and all-agree buckets at modest edges (0.033-0.073 observed in recent decisions). Tightening to 0.07 raises the bar and should filter out more marginal momentum entries, aligning with the mostly-breakeven realized edge after fees.

diagnosis: The bot is roughly break-even overall (50.7% win rate, -$68.37 across 404 trades) with the entire loss concentrated in the MOMENTUM setup (-$55.81 over 383 trades, 49% win) and ARB_LEG (-$18.45 over 8 trades). ARB itself is strongly profitable (92% win, +$5.89) but under-utilized (only 13 trades). The core problem is that momentum entries are being taken on weak/moderate signals (move 10-20bps bucket is a validated -$33.47 money-loser at 28/81=35% win rate) and the lesson veto is already correctly suppressing new move10-20 trades in recent decisions — this is working as intended and should be kept. However, 'left60-120' (-$20.25, 36% win) and 'price<0.45' (-$19.54, 31% win) are also validated losers but are NOT appearing as active vetoes in the recent decision log, suggesting they may not be fully armed/enforced, or trades in that bucket are still slipping through from other paths (e.g., stop-loss triggered exits are dominating, several stop-losses hit at 0.19-0.25 bid very close to entry, suggesting momentum reversals happen fast after entry). Coin-level performance is uneven: doge (-$23.45, 39% win) and eth (-$25.40, 54% win but large losses) are the biggest drags, while btc is the only solidly profitable coin (+$10.83, 60% win). The 'all-agree' peer bucket is surprisingly a loser (-$18.99 over 112 trades, action=reduce_confidence already flagged) — high peer agreement is not predictive of success here, likely because peer agreement proxies for a broad market move that the 5-min window can't capitalize on before reversal. The 'left120+' bucket is the only solid structural edge (+$10.77, 50.3% win over 175 trades) meaning earlier entries with more time remaining perform better than late entries. Recent decisions show heavy and repeated vetoing of xrp/doge/sol entries on move10-20, indicating the lesson system is now actively filtering ~40-50% of signals, which is good, but the bot is still entering trades on moderate edges (0.04-0.09) in the 0.55-0.65 ask range that historically have close to coinflip outcomes once fees are applied.
